title: Huddle: Evals preflight notes — optimize + A/B follow-ups
summary: Prep notes for quick huddle to triage the small quality regression seen in A/B on customer prompt set C. Goal: agree on immediate mitigations + 7-day experimentation plan.
notes:
Context:
- Yesterday's A/B (traffic split 50/50) on customer prompt set C showed a median answer-quality drop of ~4.6% (eval metric: rouge_l-like proprietary score) for model variant B (quantized q4_0, small kernel changes). Host config was standard (dedicated pool: dp-prod-3).
- Signal surfaced via automated quality monitor (alert id REDINF-821) and customer QA slack thread (#cust-c-evals). No infra outages. Latency and throughput within SLO.

Agenda (15 min):
1) Quick readout of metrics and concrete diffs (Aisha) — 4m
2) Hypotheses + evidence (all) — 4m
3) Triage plan: immediate rollback vs targeted prompt fixes vs canary tweak (Priya) — 3m
4) Assign experiments + owners (Diego/Jonah) — 4m

Quick findings / raw numbers:
- Eval subset: prompt-set-C-top500 (customer-supplied).
- Baseline (variant A): median score 0.782. Variant B: 0.746. Delta: -0.036 absolute (~4.6% relative).
- Failure modes (manual spot checks): hallucinations on multi-step instructions, missing key constraints (e.g., timeframe), subtle formatting changes (lists -> paragraphs).
- Token-level cost: variant B slightly cheaper (~3% token cost) due to q4 quantization, but user-facing quality loss > cost win.

Hypotheses:
H1: Quantization-induced numerical instability at long sequence lengths causing degraded attention alignment on constraint tokens.
  - Evidence: regressions concentrate on prompts with >280 tokens.
  - Quick check: compare kv-cache differences on a failing example (diego to run kv-diff script).
H2: Kernel selection fallback path for the new conv-attn op introduced in PR #412 regresses edge-case formatting.
  - Evidence: offline inference with older kernel set reproduces baseline behavior on failing prompts.
H3: Prompt set interaction with new bias-correction tweak in reranker stage (optimize v0.9.3) reduces weight on constraint tokens.
  - Evidence: reranker logits distribution shifted slightly in top-k window. Need Jonah to dump reranker scores for sample range.

Immediate mitigation options (pros/cons):
- Full rollback to variant A (safe, quick) — PROS: fast fix; CONS: loses cost savings, needs deploy rollback ticket and customer comms.
- Targeted rollback: revert quantization only, keep kernel changes — PROS: preserves some perf; CONS: risk of partial incompatibilities.
- Prompt shim on customer's side: add explicit constraint rewording (short-term patch) — PROS: no infra change; CONS: customer effort + patchy coverage.
- Canary narrowing: reduce traffic to variant B to 10% and keep running diagnostics — PROS: buys time; CONS: still exposes some customers.

Decision proposal (what I want from huddle):
- Do a 10% canary reduction immediately (Priya to change routing) AND schedule full rollback plan if no micro-fixes in 48 hours.
- Prioritize two short experiments: kv-cache diff + reranker logits dump + local re-run with unquantized weights.

Experiments (each should produce reproducible artifacts + one-line pass/fail):
E1 (Diego): Run kv-diff on 50 failing prompts; compare attention weights and cached keys between A and B. Command: "python tools/kv_diff.py --model a=/models/redwood-v1-7b --model b=/models/redwood-v1-7b-q4_0 --inputs data/promptset-c/sample50.jsonl --out s3://redwood-evals/tmp/kv-diff-0728"
E2 (Jonah): Dump reranker scores for sample range 200-400 and compute top-k shift. Script: "scripts/dump_reranker.sh rerank-prod v0.9.3 200 400 > /tmp/rerank-dump.txt"
E3 (Priya/Aisha): Canary tweak + small customer communication. Reduce variant B traffic from 50% -> 10% and post a short note in #cust-c-evals. Rollback steps documented in REDINF-822.
E4 (Aisha): Local run unquantized weights with same kernels to check if quantization is the main factor. Use eval-run tool with --no-quantize flag.

Data & infra checks (SRE):
- Verify no GPU OOMs during A/B window (site reliability to confirm; Jonah filing a watch).
- Confirm streaming chunking/version mismatch not responsible (check embed API versions).

Rollout / rollback plan:
- If canary at 10% still shows >2% median regression after 48h on prompt-set-C, trigger immediate full rollback. Owner: Priya. Escalation path: oncall-eng -> eng-shiproom.
- Customer comms: Diego to draft see-what-we-found note; Aisha to approve.

Open questions / blockers: 
- Do we have freeze snapshots for kernels used on previous deploy? (Jonah)
- Can we reproduce the failure deterministically in local smaller seed? (Diego)
- Is the reranker change independent of quantization? (Priya)

Action items (owner — due):
- Priya: reduce traffic to variant B to 10% and create REDINF-822 rollback ticket — due 2026-07-28 17:00 PT.
- Diego: run E1 kv-diff on sample50 and upload artifacts to s3; post short summary in thread — due 2026-07-29 12:00 PT.
- Jonah: dump reranker scores (E2) and attach raw logs to PR 412 discussion — due 2026-07-29 12:00 PT.
- Aisha: run local unquantized check (E4) and write short note on whether quantization alone reproduces regression — due 2026-07-29 09:00 PT.
- Diego + Aisha: draft customer-facing note if rollback needed (1st draft) — due 2026-07-29 18:00 PT.

Post-huddle follow up plan:
- 24h checkpoint (quick async update in #optimize-evals): everyone posts a 1-line update.
- 48h decision: if any experiment shows definitive root cause -> implement fix; else roll back.
- Capture final RCA in confluence page and link to JIRA.

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Keep record of any prompt-engineering patches we suggest to customers; don't leak internal reranker details.
- Preserve sample IDs used for debugging so we can replay in reproduce pipeline.
- Check whether recent kernel selector metric (selector-confidence) spiked during deploy time (may point to fallback path).
